sessions.title: PowerShell DBA Dream dbatools Workshop
sessions.description: This full day class will take you through the most essential DBATOOLS module commands and teach you all you need to know to hit the ground running. We will go over the dbatools ecosystem and the common concepts that will help you get the most out of this module. There are over 650 commands, so we won't be going over all of them, but I will take you through the mainstream, daily use commands in the Get, Set, Test, Backup, Restore and others in the verbs in this module. Not only that but we will cover how to prepare your profile and environment to have ready variables that will assist you in quick commandline operation as well as automated running of commands. Join me in the quest for becoming a PowerShell DBA.

sessions.title: AI for the Rest of Us: Vibe Coding & Building MCP Servers with FastMCP
sessions.description:
You've heard the buzzwords — AI, LLMs, vectors, embeddings, "MCP" — but you've
  never actually sat down and built anything with them. This hands-on day is
  for you. No AI experience required, and you don't even need to be a developer.
 
  We'll start at the very beginning: what AI and large language models actually
  are, what a "vector" and an "embedding" really mean, and how a vector store
  (yes, including SQL Server 2025) fits into the picture. Then we'll get our
  hands dirty with "vibe coding" — using AI to build small, working tools live,
  breaking things and fixing them as we go. In the afternoon we level up to
  FastMCP: what the Model Context Protocol is, how to find and use MCP tools,
  and how to build your own so an AI can take real actions — like querying a
  database in plain English.

  This is a workshop, not a lecture. We introduce a concept, then you build it.
  You won't walk out with a polished product — you'll walk out with something
  better: a real understanding of how modern AI fits together, and the
  confidence to go build your own.

  What you'll learn
  - What LLMs, vectors, embeddings, and vector stores actually are — in plain
  English
  - How to "vibe code" working tools with AI, and what to do when it breaks
  - What MCP and FastMCP are, and how to find, use, and build your own MCP tools
  - How to get an AI to take real actions (like working with a database) safely

  What you'll leave with
  - A clear mental model of how modern AI systems fit together
  - Hands-on experience building (and breaking) things with AI
  - Your first MCP tool — and the confidence to keep going

  What to bring (prerequisites)
  - A laptop (Windows 11+, MacOS M1+) with the workshop environment installed
  ahead of time — we'll send setup instructions before the event so you arrive
  ready to build
  - Curiosity. That's it — no prior AI or coding experience needed.

sessions.title: Data on Fire: A Hands-On Intro to Spark in Fabric
sessions.description:
Curious about Apache Spark but not sure where to start? This hands-on session introduces you to Spark in Microsoft Fabric Notebooks—a powerful and accessible way to process and analyze big data using familiar tools in the Microsoft ecosystem.

We’ll break down key Spark concepts like distributed computing, DataFrames, and lazy evaluation, then show how they come to life inside Fabric’s notebook experience. You’ll see practical demos that cover loading, transforming, and analyzing large datasets—while leveraging Fabric’s modern data stack, including OneLake, Dataflows, and Pipelines.

You’ll also learn how to choose between Spark and pure Python notebooks in Fabric, based on execution needs, data integration, and use case fit.

Whether you're a SQL pro, BI developer, or data engineer, this session will give you the tools and confidence to start using Spark in your own projects—no cluster management required.

sessions.title: From Problem to Solution: Analytics Consulting in the Age of AI
sessions.description: What does it actually take to guide an organization from a messy, undefined problem to a solution they can act on? In this session, our team will share our typical roadmap for organizations looking to evolve their data landscape while truly allowing their data to work for them and not against them. We're sharing client stories, how the work is evolving, and how our team works to support clients as they move toward Artificial Intelligence

sessions.title: Creating a Career Roadmap and Owning Your Job Search
sessions.description: This session will help to empower IT professionals to think strategically about how to make the most of their current role, and how to reach their ultimate career goals.

sessions.title: Master AI prompts by creating a load tester
sessions.description: Join me in building a load-testing platform with Python.  The backend DB is Postgres.  I’ll walk through the prompts I used, the pitfalls I encountered, and the problems that come with working with AI to get a usable application out of it.  This presentation will both walk you through the use of AI prompts and teach you key things you need to know when working with AI

sessions.title: Demystifying Agentic Software
sessions.description:
With all the hype surrounding AI and agentic software, it can be hard to tell what's real and what's marketing. AI companies are incentivized to sell us a version of reality that isn't here yet, and with the landscape shifting weekly, even the current state is a moving target.

In this talk we (and by we, I mean Claude) will start with a local LLM doing raw text prediction and build up to an agentic loop that can call tools. While I make no promises that this agent will do anything useful, along the way we'll develop a mental model for how agents actually work, how to evaluate what they produce, and how to bias them toward the outcomes we want.

sessions.title: AI Ready with Microsoft Purview and Fabric
sessions.description:
Managing data across large organizations can feel like an endless game of catch-up. Microsoft Purview and Fabric make it easier by giving teams tools to organize, protect, and share data without constant compliance headaches.

First, we’ll look at the challenges organizations face when data is scattered across silos with possible security gaps slowing everything down and creating possible regulatory concerns. 

Next, we’ll see how Purview and Fabric work to streamline data management by cataloging assets, enforcing protections, and making data easier to find. 

Finally, we’ll show how this approach simplifies compliance, improves data accessibility, and supports better collaboration across teams.

Attendees will come away with a practical guide on using Microsoft Purview and Fabric to keep data organized, compliant, and useful.

sessions.title: From Data to Decisions: Building Agentic Construction Intelligence with Databricks Agent Bricks
sessions.description:
Construction companies generate massive amounts of operational and financial data across ERP systems, field reports, inspection logs, and project controls tools. Yet most organizations still rely on dashboards and manual investigation to understand project performance.
This session demonstrates how agentic workflows built with Databricks Agent Bricks transform construction data into automated operational intelligence. Using a synthetic construction services scenario, we show how multiple AI agents analyze project financials, field inspections, and operational data stored in the lakehouse.
Specialized agents interpret structured ERP data and unstructured inspection documents, while a supervisor agent orchestrates investigations across multiple sources to detect cost variance, identify recurring defects, and recommend operational actions. The demo illustrates how the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform enables governed, explainable automation while preserving enterprise data governance.
Attendees will learn practical design patterns for building agent-driven systems that move construction analytics beyond dashboards toward actionable intelligence.

sessions.title: SQL Server Security Myths: What Actually Matters in Real Environments
sessions.description:
Many SQL Server environments appear secure at first glance. TDE is enabled, sa is disabled, auditing is configured, and the number of sysadmins may even be small.

But those controls do not automatically mean the environment is defensible. Real-world SQL Server risk often hides in privilege escalation paths, over-permissioned database roles, SQL Agent configuration, weak operational boundaries, and assumptions that nobody has tested.

In this session, we will walk through common SQL Server security myths and compare the perception of safety with the actual risk. You will learn which controls genuinely reduce attack paths and blast radius, which ones are often misunderstood, and what to check first when assessing a SQL Server environment.

sessions.title: Demystifying Microsoft Fabric: Architecture and Organization 101
sessions.description:
As with any other new technology, Microsoft Fabric comes with a host of new terms and concepts.  Do you know your tenants from your capacities from your workspaces?  How about your data lakes from your delta lakes and your lakehouses from your warehouses?  If not, you're not alone!

This session is aimed at data analysts, on-premises data professionals, managers/executives, and other tech pros struggling to understand the purpose, architecture, and organization of Fabric.  We'll use plain English and not marketing-speak or technobabble to ensure all attendees have a shared understanding of this new paradigm for analytics in the Microsoft ecosystem.

sessions.title: Learning PostgreSQL as a SQL Server User
sessions.description:
More and more organizations are hosting their data on multiple platforms. One of the fastest growing relational platforms is PostgreSQL. While the root behaviors of tables and relationships between them are the same, there remains a very distinct set of differences between PostgreSQL and other platforms.

If you've been a SQL Server user, developer, DBA, and your organization is now adding PostgreSQL to the mix, you may have a somewhat steep learning curve ahead. This session is meant to reduce the size of that hill you're going to climb as you add PostgreSQL skills. We'll cover the common aspects of both platforms, the subtle differences between the two, and, of course, some of the unique behaviors to separates PostgreSQL from SQL Server. You'll get a good introduction to the core behaviors of PostgreSQL and the appropriate language to use when working with that data platform. All of this is designed to flatten out that learning curve and get you started supporting PostgreSQL just as well as you currently support SQL Server.

sessions.title: Getting Started with DuckDB
sessions.description: DuckDB is a lightweight, open-source database that has become a go-to solution for running analytical queries on local machines. In this talk, we will explore why that is, showing off some of its simplicity, portability, and extensibility. We will investigate how its columnar data storage helps with analytical queries and how to read data in common file formats such as CSV, JSON, and Parquet. We will also dig into its SQL interface and see how closely it mirrors relational database solutions. By the end of this talk, we will understand some of the best use cases for DuckDB and what it takes to get started.

sessions.title: Zero to App Store
sessions.description:
The barrier between "having an idea" and "launching an app" has officially vanished. In this high-energy, 60-minute session, we’ll prove that you don't need a computer science degree to become a published developer. Leveraging the power of AI coding assistants like Claude Code, Gemini, and ChatGPT, we will demonstrate how to transform natural language into functional applications ready for the iOS, Android, and Windows stores.

Whether you want to build specialized cybersecurity tools, productivity apps, or personal projects, this workshop teaches you the "vibe coding" workflow: using AI to handle the heavy lifting of syntax while you focus on design and logic. We will skip the complex IDE setups and dive straight into building, debugging, and the roadmap to getting your first app into the hands of users worldwide.

sessions.title: PowerShell + AI: Enhancement, Not Replacement
sessions.description:
Lets explore how to effectively integrate AI tools into your PowerShell development workflow without losing sight of what really matters: solid scripting fundamentals. This session shows you where AI can genuinely help with things like rapid prototyping and learning new concepts but also reveals the common traps that can bite you in production, from security holes to missing error handling that AI just doesn’t catch.

Through live demos and real-world examples, you’ll see a practical approach that uses AI to speed up the boring stuff while relying on your expertise to make sure everything actually works when it counts. We’ll cover specific techniques for writing better prompts, validating AI-generated code, and building review processes that catch problems before they become expensive mistakes. By the end, you’ll have concrete strategies you can use right away, and a clear understanding of why your PowerShell knowledge is actually more important now, not less, in a world where anyone can generate code in seconds.

sessions.title: Ranking FizzBuzz for Fun Not Profit
sessions.description: Ah Fizzbuzz, a staple of dev interview ghost stories, always lurking around the corner, rarely actually seen in the wild. But I want to talk about it. For the last decade I've been collecting fun and unusual FizzBuzz implementations over a variety of programming languages. Lets go over them with a good ol' fashioned S-tier ranking. The best one will shock and amaze you!

sessions.title: Azure Storage: You want to put what where?
sessions.description:
Migrating to the cloud should not be considered a cost saving measure, but there are a number of tricks and tips you can use to make sure your business' hard-earned money is used to optimize your storage choices for all of your Azure choices. 

Join me with an in-depth discussion on your choices in storage for SQL Server on Azure VM, Azure SQL Managed Instance (MI), and Azure SQL along with a little bit of discussion about HA/DR/and BC.  

Bring ALL your questions and sample scenarios so we can come up with a plan to provide your Azure installation with the perfect storage for your business needs!

sessions.title: Introduction to Microsoft Fabric Variable Library: Simplifying CI/CD Automation
sessions.description: Discover how Microsoft Fabric’s Variable Library simplifies CI/CD automation by centralizing and securing environment-specific values. In this introductory session, you’ll learn what a Variable Library is, why it matters, and how to use it effectively in deployment pipelines. We’ll explore practical scenarios, best practices for managing variables, and tips for governance and security. Whether you’re new to Fabric or looking to streamline your workflows, this session will help you unlock the power of variable management.

sessions.title: Transactions Are Events: Event-Driven Architecture On Data In Motion
sessions.description: You may have seen Real-time Intelligence and thought "that's cool, but I don't have any streaming data". What we all have, though, is transactions. Lots of them. That means we have data moving around our ecosystem, likely with traditional ETL jobs and schedulers. Come learn how change data capture, change event streaming, and Real-time Intelligence combine to give you the tools to create a truly event-driven (and less fragile) data architecture.

sessions.title: Careers in IT Baton Rouge 2026
sessions.description: Careers in IT will feature a panel of industry leaders and experts who directly interact with participants in a moderated question and answer session. This will allow participants to gain insight into what the IT community sees as valuable (skill-sets, certifications, experience, and etc) so that they can be better prepared for a career transition or to start work in the IT field for the first time.

sessions.title: Keynote: The Nature of Work in the Age of AI: Prevailing When the Brain Meets the Machine
sessions.description: Lots of visuals, examples, and will cross-cut all audiences. I have seen so much despair, anxiety and confusion in our industry -- software engineers, corporate professionals, and even professors as the news of the impact of AI is hitting them. This talk will educate, empower, and inspire our SQL Saturday/Day of Date audience.

sessions.title: SQL in the Fabric Era: Translate existing skills into the modern data platform
sessions.description:
SQL pros, meet Fabric! This session shares hands-on examples of SQL database in Fabric in action with analytics, governance, and Power BI integration included.

We will take a look at using the OLTP database, the SQL Analytics endpoint, and mirroring work to enable integration with other Fabric workloads in a way that is intuitive to SQL Pros. We will also explore how some of the built-in governance features of Fabric aide SQL developers and DBAs alike.

By the end of this session you will better understand how to extend your SQL skills into a modern data ecosystem without leaving your comfort zone.

sessions.title: The Engineering Leaders Test
sessions.description:
The Engineering Leaders Test: Would You Rejoin Your Own Team? How aspiring leaders can build teams they’d be proud to come back to. 
Practical ideas on how to self-reflect on your team and move forward building trust and teamwork.

sessions.title: Intro to PowerShell with dbatools for the DBA
sessions.description: Whether you manage a single instance of SQL Server or hundreds of them, PowerShell and dbatools are invaluable additions to your toolbox. Today, we’re going to scratch the surface with what you can do with these tools to simplify, automate and standardize some of the tasks you perform.

sessions.title: Local AI for .NET
sessions.description:
In this session, we’ll introduce Foundry Local, a lightweight runtime that lets you run AI models locally and call them from your .NET applications — no prior AI experience required.

We’ll start by answering the basics: What is Foundry Local, how does it work, and why should .NET developers care? Then, we’ll build a real C# application that uses Foundry Local for tasks like text generation, summarization, and structured responses. You’ll learn how to install Foundry Local, call it from C#, handle responses, and integrate AI features into real applications.

You’ll walk away with a working sample project and a clear understanding of how Foundry Local fits into modern .NET development so you can start experimenting with AI in your own applications.

sessions.title: Beyond the Hype: Practical NFT Use Cases for Data and Analytics
sessions.description:
NFTs have moved well beyond digital collectibles and are increasingly being explored for real-world applications like credentialing, asset tracking, and data provenance. But how do they actually work, and what does it take to create one?

In this session, we will break down the architecture behind NFTs and walk through minting one step by step on a test blockchain network. You will see how metadata, decentralized storage (IPFS), and smart contracts come together and how these concepts map to familiar data engineering principles like schema design, data integrity, and system architecture.

We will also explore practical use cases relevant to data professionals, including issuing verifiable course certificates and tracking digital assets. By the end of the session, you will understand not just how to mint an NFT, but when it makes sense to use one and when it does not. Attendees will leave with a repeatable workflow they can experiment with immediately.

sessions.title: Beyond “Set and Forget”: Mastering the Ola Hallengren Maintenance Solution
sessions.description:
The Ola Hallengren Maintenance Solution is installed on thousands of SQL Server instances, yet most environments rely on default jobs and hope for the best. While those defaults work, they rarely align with real-world workloads, availability requirements, or maintenance windows.

In this session, we’ll go beyond “set and forget” and break down how the Ola solution actually works—and how to tune it intentionally. You’ll learn how the backup, integrity check, and index maintenance procedures make decisions, and how to control that behavior using parameters, schedules, and execution context.

We’ll also explore the built-in logging tables and return codes, showing how to use them for troubleshooting, reporting, and automation—turning maintenance from a black box into an observable, auditable process.

You’ll leave with solid guidance on how to redesign existing Ola jobs into a flexible, scalable maintenance framework that supports performance, reliability, and growth—without rewriting everything from scratch.

sessions.title: From Operational Data to Insights: An Agentic AI Assistant for DevOps Intelligence
sessions.description:
Modern DevOps environments generate vast volumes of operational data across logs, monitoring systems, documentation, and collaboration platforms, yet much of this data remains underutilized due to fragmentation and lack of real-time accessibility. This session explores an agentic AI-powered DevOps Knowledge Assistant that transforms disparate operational data into actionable insights. Leveraging natural language processing, agent-based workflows, and microservices architecture, the system unifies structured and unstructured data to deliver context-aware responses and automate routine tasks.

We examine how integrating logs, runbooks, and historical incident data enables faster query resolution, improved incident response, and data-driven decision-making. The session also covers implementation strategies, including secure data integration, governance, and user adoption. Results demonstrate significant gains in troubleshooting efficiency, onboarding, and cross-team collaboration. By evolving toward predictive analytics, this approach highlights how organizations can unlock the full value of operational data to enhance resilience, efficiency, and intelligent automation in DevOps.

sessions.title: The Age of Agentic Engineering in SDLC
sessions.description: Software engineering is shifting fast — AI now plans, writes, tests, and ships code. This session looks at the spectrum from vibe coding to agentic engineering, how the SDLC is changing, and the skills and economics that matter now. We’ll close with a live demo of building a feature the agentic engineering way.

sessions.title: From Prompt to Production: AI Across Traditional and Low-Code Development
sessions.description:
Artificial Intelligence is doing far more than generating code—it is fundamentally changing how modern software is designed, developed, tested, deployed, and maintained. Whether you're building enterprise applications with Java and .NET or delivering solutions on low-code platforms like ServiceNow, AI is becoming an essential member of the development team.

In this session, we'll explore how Generative AI is reshaping the entire Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC), from turning business requirements into user stories and architecture decisions to generating code, creating automated tests, reviewing pull requests, improving documentation, and accelerating deployment. We'll compare how these capabilities apply in both traditional software engineering and low-code development, demonstrating that AI is not replacing developers—it is enabling them to focus on higher-value problem solving.

Through practical demonstrations and real-world examples, attendees will see how AI can accelerate delivery, improve software quality, and reduce repetitive work while also learning where human expertise remains critical. We'll discuss best practices for validating AI-generated solutions, maintaining security and governance, and integrating AI responsibly into enterprise development workflows.

Whether you're a developer, architect, ServiceNow professional, technical leader, or simply curious about the future of software engineering, you'll leave with actionable techniques and a practical framework for adopting AI across your own development process.

sessions.title: Power Query Escape Room
sessions.description:
The Plot:
For the first time ever, the villainous Lord Taart Chart has emerged from the shadows, and he’s targeting your data! In a brazen attack, he’s stolen your carefully curated data and locked it deep inside his fortified Azure Vault.

Your Mission:
You and your team must rise to the challenge, confronting Lord Taart Chart’s wicked ways by solving his 10 Power Query Puzzles. These devious challenges will test your ability to wrangle, transform, and tame even the messiest of data.
Can your team prove its Power Query skills and outsmart this foe before your data is lost forever?

sessions.title: Intention Is All You Need: Maintaining Agency in a World of Agents
sessions.description:
As AI systems increasingly act on our behalf, writing, deciding, and executing tasks, the promise is clear: greater efficiency, more output, less effort. But this raises an important question. What are we optimizing for? 

This talk challenges the assumption that more automation is always better. Instead, it establishes AI as a tool for focusing on what matters most. Rather than maximizing productivity at any cost, we can responsibly delegate tasks to automation in ways that support what matters most to us. The session will focus on the skills required to (1) make effective decisions about how AI is used in practice, (2) determine what to delegate and what to retain based on what we care about, and (3) guide AI systems without becoming dependent on them.  As AI capabilities increase, the challenge isn’t simply to keep up. We must remain intentional about what we choose to optimize and why.

sessions.title: Optimizing CI/CD for Hybrid and Cloud Environments with DevOps and AI
sessions.description:
As AI becomes increasingly integrated into software development, optimizing CI/CD pipelines for hybrid and cloud environments requires a balance between automation, security, and governance. This session explores how to leverage DevOps best practices and tools to build scalable, secure, and AI-enhanced CI/CD solutions that support the entire development lifecycle—from code commit to production deployment.

We’ll cover key DevOps principles, recommended tools for automation, testing, and deployment, as well as strategies for integrating AI-driven capabilities to enhance efficiency, detect anomalies, and improve decision-making. Additionally, we’ll discuss how to mitigate AI-related vulnerabilities in the DevOps pipeline, ensuring model integrity, data security, and compliance. Attendees will learn how to implement GitOps, Infrastructure as Code (IaC), and progressive delivery techniques while maintaining control over AI-powered automation. Whether you're incorporating AI into your CI/CD workflows or securing an existing pipeline, this session will provide actionable insights to streamline development while minimizing risks.

sessions.title: A Beginner's Guide to Wrangling Asynchronicity in JavaScript
sessions.description: In this talk, Raymond will talk about how to handle asynchronous code in JavaScript applications. He'll demonstrate the problems you encounter, the older style solutions (callbacks), and show how to use promises and async/await to make your code easier to work with. This will be a beginner's level topic with a focus on *practical* use cases but will wrap up with links to more solutions and advanced discussion.

sessions.title: Implementing Data Gateway High Availability and Redundancy
sessions.description: The on‑premises data gateway is a critical dependency for Power BI, Power Platform, and Microsoft Fabric—but when deployed as a single server, it becomes a hidden single point of failure. In this session, you’ll learn how to design and operate a highly available and disaster‑resilient gateway architecture using Microsoft‑supported clustering. We’ll cover core concepts such as gateway instances, nodes, and clusters; explain how gateway failover works; discuss platform limitations and tradeoffs; and demonstrate how PowerShell supports enterprise‑scale gateway management.

sessions.title: AI Made Us Faster. Data Makes Us Smarter.
sessions.description:
AI made teams faster, but faster creation does not automatically create better decisions, trusted answers, or safer delivery. This talk explores why data teams are becoming essential to the AI software delivery lifecycle by turning definitions, quality rules, lineage, governance, and data contracts into controls that shape AI behavior.

Attendees will see how data moves from downstream reporting into the delivery workflow, and how changing a data contract can change what an AI system is allowed to know, use, explain, and prove.

This is the third talk in a series about how AI is changing the software delivery workflow and why the roles around engineering must move closer to how software is built, released, governed, and improved:

AI Made Us Faster. Why Aren’t We Delivering Faster?
AI Made Us Faster. Security Must Make Delivery Safer.
AI Made Us Faster. Data Must Make Delivery Smarter.

sessions.title: Guardians of the Data Galaxy: Securing SQL Server the Right Way
sessions.description: SQL Server security isn’t a single feature — it’s a layered strategy. In this 200‑level session, we’ll walk through SQL Server’s full security stack from the outside in, starting with physical and network boundaries and moving all the way to encryption, permissions, auditing, and row‑level security. You’ll learn how each layer contributes to a defense‑in‑depth model, how attackers typically try to bypass weak configurations, and which built‑in SQL Server features can close those gaps quickly. Whether you manage production workloads, support developers, or design data platforms, this session will give you a clear roadmap for securing SQL Server environments with practical, real‑world guidance you can apply immediately.

sessions.title: Using Data API Builder to Speed Up Application Development
sessions.description: The Data API Builder from Microsoft, you can quickly and easily expose your database objects for developers to use without writing a lot of data access layer code. In this session, we will see how to setup, configure, and use the Data API Builder and GraphQL to expose and query data in SQL Server and PostgreSQL. Learn how easy it is to run this service alongside your application and let developers filter, sort, and change data using standard GraphQL queries.

sessions.title: Git Good: GitHub and GitHub Actions for the Rest of Us
sessions.description:
LLMs are changing how we write code, manage infrastructure, and ship software, making source code management and DevOps skills more valuable than ever. If DevOps has always seemed confusing or mysterious, you're not alone. In this session, you will: 

- Learn Git and GitHub basics for storing and managing your code
- Get comfortable collaborating in repositories
- Use GitHub Actions to automate code, cloud, and database deployments
- How GitHub Actions are basically just shell scripts
- Understand how to ship software faster with fewer problems

You'll leave ready to automate, collaborate, and deliver your projects with confidence.

sessions.title: Basics of connecting REST APIs to Power BI
sessions.description:
Automated refreshes are critical to the success of many reporting solutions.  Most developers prefer connecting to databases or data warehouses where they have control over the resource allocation and transformation of the data all before it reaches Power BI.  But what happens when you do not have direct access to the database?  What happens if the data is hosted by a 3rd party cloud platform?  What if you ask for a way to get the data and they send you documentation on their APIs and say good luck?

If you have asked these questions, then this session is designed specifically for you.  We will walk you through the basics of understanding API documentation and show you how to connect with the Web connector in Power BI.  We will also cover some of the basic transformations you can perform to make your queries more efficient and highlight some of the blockers you might encounter.  We will even build a function with an API and apply it to a dataset. 

At the end of this session, you will feel comfortable using REST APIs as a data source and building connections using best practices.

sessions.title: GUMBO: The Recipe for Career Success, Personal Growth and Meaningful Work
sessions.description:
Success is a lot like a great Louisiana gumbo - there is no single recipe, but the right ingredients make all the difference.

Whether you're a student preparing for your first career opportunity, a data professional solving complex problems, a project manager leading teams, or an IT specialist navigating constant change, long-term success requires more than technical skills alone. It requires a foundation of personal growth, a clear understanding of what makes you unique, a focus on meaningful outcomes, strong connections with others, and the willingness to take ownership of your future.

In this engaging and interactive session, Tanya Boyd uses Louisiana's most iconic dish as a practical framework for career development and personal well-being. Through real-world stories, relatable examples, audience participation, and measurable strategies, participants will explore how the GUMBO framework can help them build a more fulfilling career while creating a recipe for success that is uniquely their own.

By attending this session, participants will be able to:

- Identify the five ingredients of the GUMBO framework: Growth, Uniqueness, Meaningful Outcomes, Belonging, and Ownership.
- Evaluate their personal and professional strengths using the GUMBO self-assessment model.
- Apply measurable strategies to support career development, skill growth, and personal well-being.
- Recognize how relationships, purpose, and accountability contribute to long-term success.
- Develop a personalized action plan to strengthen at least one area of their own GUMBO recipe.

sessions.title: Power BI API: Automating the Analytics Lifecycle
sessions.description:
Take your Power BI solutions beyond the Desktop! In this session, we’ll dive into advanced use cases for the Power BI REST API, showcasing how to automate your workflow, streamline your development, and integrate into your custom portals. Learn how to automate report deployment, create personalized experiences with row-level security, and leverage real-time data updates to keep your visuals fresh.

Whether you’re building internal tools or client-facing applications, this session will provide actionable insights and practical examples to help you unlock the full potential of the Power BI API. Join us to supercharge your analytics solutions!

sessions.title: Fabric Unified Admin & Monitoring (FUAM)  aka.ms/FUAM
sessions.description: Deploying and Utilizing Fabric Admin & Monitoring for the Data Engineering and Database Admin or Power BI / Fabric Admin.  aka.ms/FUAM

sessions.title: Fabric SQL Database: Simplifying OLTP and Real-Time Analytics
sessions.description:
Managing transactional workloads while enabling analytics in near real-time often requires complex architectures and multiple tools. SQL Database in Microsoft Fabric, currently in preview, aims to simplify this by combining OLTP capabilities with built-in analytics integration.

This session introduces SQL Database in Fabric—a developer-friendly, cloud-native solution built on Azure SQL that automatically replicates data into OneLake for near real-time analytics.  You'll learn how it supports familiar tools like SQL Server Management Studio and the Fabric portal, offers intelligent performance features, and enables cross-database queries and semantic modeling for Power BI.

Attendees will leave with a clear understanding of how Fabric SQL can streamline data architecture, reduce operational overhead, and accelerate insights—all without sacrificing transactional performance.
 
Session Goals - Attendees will:
 
Understand the problem SQL database in Fabric is solving in modern data architectures.

Learn how SQL database in Fabric integrates OLTP and analytics through OneLake replication.

Explore supported development tools and intelligent performance features.
Compare SQL database in Fabric with Azure SQL to understand trade-offs and use cases.

See live demos of database creation, connection, and analytics endpoint usage.

sessions.title: AI Agents That Don't Make Things Up: Grounding with Fabric IQ, Semantic Models, and Guardrails
sessions.description: Your Data Agent just told the CFO that Q3 revenue was $47 million. The real number was $74 million. The decimals were right. The meaning was wrong. And now nobody trusts the AI — or the team that built it. This is the grounding problem, and it's the #1 reason enterprise AI pilots fail. The fix isn't a better model or a cleverer prompt. It's giving your agent a shared understanding of what your data actually means. In this session, I'll show you how Microsoft Fabric solves this with three layers of grounding: semantic models that define your business metrics, ontologies that map your business vocabulary, and agent instructions that set guardrails on what the AI can and can't do. You'll see a live demo of a Data Agent that hallucinates — then watch as we ground it step by step until it gives trusted, auditable answers. If you're building AI agents (or being asked to), this is the session that keeps you out of trouble.

sessions.title: When your email security work and you still get phished.
sessions.description:
Email security tools (SEG, URL rewriting, attachment sandboxing) have improved—so attackers increasingly route around the inbox. Initial access now often starts with QR codes, SMS, search ads/SEO poisoning, collaboration app lures, and “quick IT fix” prompts that never touch email filters. From there, adversaries use Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM) techniques and “ClickFix” social engineering to hijack authenticated browser sessions and reuse session tokens—making logins look normal and often bypassing MFA.

For data teams, this is a hidden risk: a compromised identity/session can grant access to cloud portals, BI workspaces, storage, and data tooling without tripping traditional “phish” alarms. The outcome isn’t only data theft—it can be data integrity damage (silent changes to reporting, pipelines, permissions, or exports) that undermines trust in dashboards and operational decisions.

This session translates post-email attacks into data-platform reality: what these compromises look like in identity logs, how to detect “successful login” events that aren’t actually safe, and a practical “last-mile” hardening roadmap that protects the point where analysts and engineers interact with cloud data.

You’ll leave with a prioritized checklist for hardening identity + admin paths, plus monitoring ideas tailored to data workloads—so your organization can keep using modern cloud analytics without betting everything on email filters.

sessions.title: SQL Server vs. Cosmos DB: The Definitive Decision Matrix
sessions.description:
"It depends" is the standard answer for database selection, but only if you understand what it depends on. For developers deciding between SQL Server and Azure Cosmos DB, understanding the differences in their internal engines is critical to performance.

In this session, we strip away the abstraction layers to compare the query engines of Microsoft's top databases. We will dive deep into the internals, comparing how each engine handles indexing, scaling, and query optimization. You will see exactly how a "simple" query executes differently in a distributed system vs. a centralized one. Come for the feature comparison; stay for the survival guide on avoiding costly migration mistakes.

sessions.title: Blogging: Lessons I Learned the Hard Way
sessions.description:
Ready to start blogging but not sure where to begin? You're not alone. Many data professionals leave conferences inspired to share their knowledge but struggle to publish that first post.
In this session, I'll share the hard lessons from my blogging journey so you can avoid common pitfalls and start writing sooner. We'll explore:
   • Choosing the right platform for your needs (pros and cons of each)
   • Alternative outlets beyond traditional blogs
   • Real examples of how blogging can boost your career and community presence
   • Practical strategies to get from "I should write about this" to hitting publish
Whether you're aiming to establish thought leadership, support your speaking goals, or simply give back to the community, this session will help you turn inspiration into action. Stop overthinking it—let's get you blogging.

sessions.title: Database Commando: Tactical Maneuvers To Protect Performance
sessions.description:
This Lighting Talk session presents practical, developer‑focused strategies for keeping SQL Server performant and auditable. It covers rapid triage techniques for poor queries, common coding patterns that cause production problems, and pragmatic approaches to detecting schema drift and unauthorized changes. The emphasis is on concise, actionable guidance developers can apply when investigating slow queries or reviewing database‑related code.
The rapid triage portion outlines which DMVs and metrics to check first, how to spot I/O hotspots, memory pressure, tempdb contention, and plan instability, and what quick indicators help prioritize fixes. The code review portion highlights high‑risk patterns to watch for, including tradeoffs between temp tables and table variables, data‑type mismatches and implicit conversions, and risky uses of CTEs, recursion, and views that can hide performance costs.
The schema monitoring portion describes lightweight auditing and alerting strategies to surface unexpected DDL activity, ways to correlate changes with deployments and authors, and practical detection techniques for schema drift without heavy operational overhead. The session is aimed at backend developers, engineers, or accidental DBAs who work with SQL Server and want focused, developer‑centric approaches to reduce surprises and improve reliability.

She has also directed enterprise-scale ServiceNow implementations, optimizing ITSM, CMDB, and Change Management processes while strengthening operational efficiency and regulatory compliance.

A certified Scrum Master and Six Sigma Yellow Belt, Renada combines technical expertise with a strategic business perspective to deliver measurable outcomes. She is a recognized advocate for low-code innovation and frequently shares insights on leveraging AI, automation, and cloud technologies to accelerate transformation, enhance customer experiences, and drive sustainable business value.

Over the last two decades, I've been on a mission to prove that data changes everything — from factory floors to patient care. As a Senior Cloud System Data Architect and Microsoft Certified Azure Solutions Architect, I bring real-world stories from industries like automotive, healthcare, and finance to the stage. But what drives me most is advocacy. I'm passionate about creating space for women in data and technology, and I use every speaking opportunity to share not just technical know-how, but the belief that this industry gets better when more diverse voices are part of the conversation.

speakers.bio:
Shankara Krishna Teja Arra is an accomplished DevOps, Cloud, and AI Enthusiast Engineer with over a decade of experience designing, automating, and managing large-scale, hybrid cloud infrastructures. With deep expertise across AWS, Azure, GCP, and OpenStack, he has led complex transformations in enterprise environments, consistently delivering high availability, resilience, and efficiency. Krishna specializes in Kubernetes, containerization, and infrastructure-as-code, leveraging tools like Terraform, Ansible, Helm, and Jenkins to streamline deployments and accelerate software delivery pipelines.

At o9 Solutions, Krishna pioneered AI-driven DevOps workflows integrating LLMs, vector databases, and conversational AI to enhance troubleshooting, automate root cause analysis, and optimize multi-cloud support operations. At Matterport, he led cloud-native architecture and CI/CD automation initiatives to improve reliability and meet demanding SLAs/SLOs.

A hackathon winner, Krishna received the o9 Hackathon Appreciation Award from Royal for an AI-driven solution, and at Ericsson he won a hackathon for simulating 5G networks on a Raspberry Pi stack.

As an open-source contributor to OpenInfra projects (including OpenStack and Airship) and to cloud-native tools such as Helm, Krishna has shared knowledge widely. He conducted a hands-on workshop on Kubernetes Operators at the annual OpenStack Summit in Shanghai, and delivered three workshops at the Dallas Cloud Computing and Kubernetes meetups one on Ansible, one on Kubernetes, and another on Terraform, Terragrunt, and Atlantis.

Known as a lifelong student, Krishna combines technical depth with curiosity, continuously exploring how AI and DevOps intersect to deliver smarter, faster, and more resilient solutions. His credentials include CKA, CKAD, Terraform Associate, GCP Associate Engineer, and AWS Developer certifications, underscoring his commitment to continuous learning and modern engineering excellence.

In his free time, Krishna enjoys experimenting with his Raspberry Pi stack building creative solutions, simulating cloud-native environments, and pushing the boundaries of edge computing for fun and learning.

Shelby Pons is a Senior Manager at EisnerAmper with a background in IT audit, accounting, ERP implementation, RPA, and data analytics. Lately, she's most focused on helping her data analytics teams serve clients creatively and effectively.

Steve Jones has been working with databases and computers for over two decades. He has worked with SQL Server since 1991, from v4.2 through SQL Server 2016. He has been a DBA, developer, and manager in a variety of large and small companies across multiple industries. In 2001 Steve founded SQLServerCentral with two partners and has been publishing technical articles and facilitating discussions among SQL Server professionals ever since. He currently is the full time editor of SQLServerCentral, as well as an evangelist for Redgate Software. Steve is a 10 year Microsoft Data Platform MVP and lives on a horse ranch in Colorado.

Tanya Boyd is a dynamic project manager, educator, and creative strategist with 20+ years of experience across disaster recovery, healthcare, IT, marketing, and government. 

As Director of Creative Collaboration at Corbeau and Project Success Academy, she blends imagination, strategy, and storytelling to design bold programs, learning experiences, and partnerships that drive measurable results. She also manages a team of PMI certification instructors who teach PMP, CAPM, and Agile certifications through PMI’s Authorized Training Partner program.

In addition to project management education, Tanya develops and delivers corporate training programs focused on communication, workplace productivity, leadership effectiveness, and practical applications of artificial intelligence. She is passionate about helping professionals leverage emerging technologies while strengthening the human skills that drive collaboration and success.

A PMP® since 2014 and PMI-ACP® since 2020, Tanya previously served as President of the PMI Baton Rouge Chapter, where she gained a front-row view of the evolving challenges facing project leaders. She also designed a three-part, seven-hour self-paced course covering the essentials of effective communication in projects.

She is a co-author of Projectland Goes to the Movies, linking pop culture to modern leadership lessons, and a contributor to the PURE Management Alliance team that created a 60-PDU professional development series.

An in-demand keynote speaker, trainer, and workshop facilitator, Tanya has delivered high-energy presentations and learning experiences to more than 50 PMI chapters, companies, and audiences at PMI Global Summit. Her topics span project leadership, communication, creativity, team development, productivity, and the practical use of AI in today's workplace.

Tanya believes curiosity and communication unlock creative solutions. Off the clock, she's often kayaking Louisiana's swamps, camera in hand, chasing the next wild idea while building her nature photography portfolio.

speakers.bio: Theresa Lubelski is passionate about helping organizations—and the people who support them—get meaningful value from Microsoft 365. She has more than 20 years of IT experience including leadership and consulting roles across healthcare, financial services, and government contracting. Her passion for collaboration technologies inspired a significant shift in her professional journey, motivating her to earn a master's degree in Teaching and Learning with Technology and dedicating her career to these innovative tools. Theresa currently drives Microsoft 365 collaboration initiatives at First Horizon Bank, with an increased emphasis on governance, security, and information architecture. She has been a speaker at Microsoft 365 community events and regional cloud conferences, where she is known for delivering practical, real‑world sessions grounded in enterprise experience.

Tony Wilhelm has amassed over two decades of experience working with databases and computers. His expertise in SQL server dates back to 1999, showcasing his extensive knowledge in the field. Throughout his career, Tony has held various roles, including DBA, developer, and manager, in both large and small companies spanning multiple industries. 

 Currently, Tony serves as a senior consultant and technical lead for the Data Management as a Service division at Moser Consulting. In this role, he brings his wealth of experience to the table, providing valuable insights and guidance to drive the implementation of effective solutions.
